sourceTitle: Goodman service manual RS6621003r3 (June 2020), 80% single-stage gas furnaces GMES80, AMES80, GCES80, ACES80, VMES80 and VCES80, troubleshooting chart
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
displayPattern: Diagnostic LED through the blower-door window on an 80% single-stage *MES80 or *CES80 furnace: Goodman GMES80 and GCES80, Amana AMES80 and ACES80, GMC VMES80 and VCES80. Count the flashes between pauses. This is not the 7-segment EE display on a 90%+ furnace.
meaning: Flame-sense signal is low. The furnace can keep running while the LED flashes seven times.
causes: Flame sensor positioned incorrectly in the burner flame
Lazy burner flame from improper gas pressure or combustion air
diySteps: Write down seven flashes. The furnace may still be heating. Do not open the burner box or sand the sensor

Technician: the chart says to sand the flame sensor, check its alignment, and compare gas pressure with the rating plate. The cautions on that row also say to clean the sensor with steel wool. Turn power off before that work
proAdvice: Seven flashes is the flame-sensor code on this chart. Three flashes is the pressure switch, not the sensor. One flash is the ignition lockout, which can also list a coated sensor after the retries are used up. Call a licensed HVAC technician. This chart is service manual RS6621003r3 for those 80% single-stage models. A 7-segment code such as EE0 or EE2 is a different furnace family.
